newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour claws back some of lead in new poll.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour claws back some of lead in new poll.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party now stands 17 points ahead of the ruling Conservatives in voting intentions for the May 1 General Election, a poll in Thursday's Times newspaper showed.

The MORI poll put support for Labour at 49 percent, unchanged from last week, while the Conservatives were down two points at 32 percent, with just two weeks to go before Britain's May 1 national election.

The poll also showed strong support for the Eurosceptics in the ruling Conservative Party, with whom Prime Minister John Major is fighting a battle over policy on the European Union's planned single currency.

Major on Wednesday issued a dramatic appeal to voters to reject the views of the Eurosceptics and remain open-minded on whether to join the proposed monetary union, so that Britain's leaders would have a free rein in the negotiations.
But the poll showed that if a referendum on Britain joining a single currency were held now, 58 percent would vote against, compared with 22 percent who said they favoured signing up.
The poll showed the public's rating of Prime Minister John Major as the most capable party leader slipped two points to 25 percent, while Labour leader Tony Blair was unchanged at 35 percent.
